paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of distance) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at integer intervals from 0 to 8. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” is linearly scaled from 0.90 to 1.05, with tick marks at 0.05 intervals. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at a value of 1.06 at 0 examples and decreasing to 0.88 at 8 examples, with a notable dip to 0.87 at 4 examples before stabilizing near 0.90. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line, remaining nearly constant at a value of approximately 1.03 across all numbers of examples from 0 to 8, with minor fluctuations between 1.02 and 1.03.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of length, with values shown on the y-axis) across varying numbers of in-context examples (on the x-axis). The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," ranges from 0 to 8 and is presented on a linear scale with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE₂₀ (←)", ranges from 0.90 to 1.05 and is also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.005. The blue line with circular markers represents the ST-ES method, starting at a value of approximately 1.06 at 0 examples, sharply decreasing to about 0.91 at 2 examples, then fluctuating slightly between approximately 0.89 and 0.91 until the final point at 8 examples, which is approximately 0.89. The orange line with square markers represents the Random method, which remains relatively stable throughout the range, starting at approximately 1.04 at 0 examples, dipping slightly to about 1.01 at 2 examples, and then fluctuating between approximately 1.01 and 1.03 until the final point at 8 examples, which is approximately 1.03.
